label: Abstract algebra

label: Category of Markov kernels
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Category of Markov kernels", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the category of Markov kernels, often denoted Stoch, is the category whose objects are measurable spaces and whose morphisms are Markov kernels.

label: Cover time
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Cover time", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the cover time of a finite Markov chain is the number of steps taken by the chain, from a given starting state, until the first step at which all states have been reached.

label: Bridgeland stability condition
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bridgeland stability condition", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, and especially algebraic geometry, a Bridgeland stability condition is an algebro-geometric stability condition defined on elements of a triangulated category.

label: Affine Grassmannian (manifold)
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Affine Grassmannian (manifold)", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, there are two distinct meanings of the term affine Grassmannian.

label: Cone condition
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Cone condition", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the cone condition is a property which may be satisfied by a subset of a Euclidean space.

label: Bourbaki–Witt theorem
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bourbaki–Witt theorem", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the Bourbaki–Witt theorem in order theory, named after Nicolas Bourbaki and Ernst Witt, is a basic fixed-point theorem for partially ordered sets.

label: Cauchy principal value
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Cauchy principal value", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the Cauchy principal value, named after Augustin-Louis Cauchy, is a method for assigning values to certain improper integrals which would otherwise be undefined.

label: Formal concept analysis
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Formal concept analysis", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In information science, formal concept analysis (FCA) is a principled way of deriving a concept hierarchy or formal ontology from a collection of objects and their properties.

sources.title: English Wikipedia article: Formal concept analysis

label: Algebraic K-theory
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Algebraic K-theory", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Algebraic K-theory is a subject area in mathematics with connections to geometry, topology, ring theory, and number theory.

label: Bernstein polynomial
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bernstein polynomial", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In the mathematical field of numerical analysis, a Bernstein polynomial is a polynomial expressed as a linear combination of Bernstein basis polynomials.

label: Decomposition of a module
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Decomposition of a module", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In abstract algebra, a decomposition of a module is a way to write a module as a direct sum of modules.

sources.title: English Wikipedia article: Decomposition of a module

label: Behrend sequence
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Behrend sequence", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In number theory, a Behrend sequence is an integer sequence whose multiples include almost all integers.

label: Global analysis
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Global analysis", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, global analysis, also called analysis on manifolds, is the study of the global and topological properties of differential equations on manifolds and vector bundles.

label: Koecher–Vinberg theorem
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Koecher–Vinberg theorem", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In operator algebra, the Koecher–Vinberg theorem is a reconstruction theorem for real Jordan algebras.

label: Chowla–Selberg formula
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Chowla–Selberg formula", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the Chowla–Selberg formula is the evaluation of a certain product of values of the gamma function at rational values in terms of values of the Dedekind eta function at imaginary quadratic irrational numbers.

label: Excision theorem
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Excision theorem", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In algebraic topology, a branch of mathematics, the excision theorem is a theorem about relative homology and one of the Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms.

label: Euler spiral
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Euler spiral", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: An Euler spiral is a curve whose curvature changes linearly with its curve length (the curvature of a circular curve is equal to the reciprocal of the radius).

label: Exponential field
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Exponential field", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, an exponential field is a field with a further unary operation that is a homomorphism from the field's additive group to its multiplicative group.

label: Epsilon calculus
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Epsilon calculus", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In logic, Hilbert's epsilon calculus is an extension of a formal language by the epsilon operator, where the epsilon operator substitutes for quantifiers in that language as a method leading to a proof of consistency for the extended formal language.

label: Harmonic tensors
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Harmonic tensors", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In this article spherical functions are replaced by polynomials that have been well known in electrostatics since the time of Maxwell and associated with multipole moments.

label: Baer norm
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Baer norm", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, in the field of group theory, the norm of a group is the intersection of the normalizers of all its subgroups.

label: Center (algebra)
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Center (algebra)", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: The term center or centre is used in various contexts in abstract algebra to denote the set of all those elements that commute with all other elements.

label: Categorical topology
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Categorical topology", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, categorical topology is an approach to topology (theory of spaces) through the concepts and methods in category theory, a branch of mathematics dealing with abstract concepts.

label: Category of measurable spaces
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Category of measurable spaces", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the category of measurable spaces, often denoted Meas, is the category whose objects are measurable spaces and whose morphisms are measurable maps.

sources.title: English Wikipedia article: Category of measurable spaces

label: Cubicity
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Cubicity", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In the mathematical field of graph theory, cubicity is a graph invariant defined to be the smallest dimension such that a graph can be realized as the intersection graph of axis-parallel unit cubes in Euclidean space.

label: Affine sphere
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Affine sphere", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In affine differential geometry, an affine sphere is a hypersurface for which the affine normals all intersect in a single point The term affine sphere is used because they play an analogous role in affine differential geometry to that of ordinary spheres in Euclidean differential geometry.

label: Bruhat order
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bruhat order", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the Bruhat order (also called the strong order, strong Bruhat order, Chevalley order, Bruhat–Chevalley order, or Chevalley–Bruhat order) is a partial order on the elements of a Coxeter group, that corresponds to the inclusion order on Schubert varieties.

label: Brouwer–Heyting–Kolmogorov interpretation
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Brouwer–Heyting–Kolmogorov interpretation", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematical logic, the Brouwer–Heyting–Kolmogorov interpretation, or BHK interpretation, is an explanation of the meaning of proof in intuitionistic logic, proposed by L. E. J. Brouwer and Arend Heyting, and independently by Andrey Kolmogorov.

label: Free lattice
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Free lattice", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, in the area of order theory, a free lattice is the free object corresponding to a lattice.

label: Bogdanov map
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bogdanov map", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In dynamical systems theory, the Bogdanov map is a chaotic 2D map related to the Bogdanov–Takens bifurcation.

label: Bernstein's constant
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bernstein's constant", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Bernstein's constant, usually denoted by the Greek letter β (beta), is a mathematical constant named after Sergei Natanovich Bernstein and is equal to 0.2801694990... .

label: Hadamard product (matrices)
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Hadamard product (matrices)", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the Hadamard product (also known as the element-wise product, entrywise product or Schur product) is a binary operation that takes in two matrices of the same dimensions and returns a matrix of the multiplied corresponding elements.

label: Bernstein–Sato polynomial
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bernstein–Sato polynomial", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the Bernstein–Sato polynomial is a polynomial related to differential operators, introduced independently by Joseph Bernstein (1971) and Mikio Sato and Takuro Shintani (1972, 1974), Sato (1990).

label: Geometric topology (object)
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Geometric topology (object)", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the geometric topology is a topology one can put on the set H of hyperbolic 3-manifolds of finite volume.

label: Krull–Akizuki theorem
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Krull–Akizuki theorem", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In commutative algebra, the Krull–Akizuki theorem states the following: Let A be a one-dimensional reduced noetherian ring, K its total ring of fractions.

label: Fáry–Milnor theorem
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Fáry–Milnor theorem", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In the mathematical theory of knots, the Fáry–Milnor theorem, named after István Fáry and John Milnor, states that three-dimensional smooth curves with small total curvature must be unknotted.

label: Hua's lemma
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Hua's lemma", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, Hua's lemma, named for Hua Loo-keng, is an estimate for exponential sums.

label: First-order logic
summary: English Wikipedia (article "First-order logic", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, philosophy, linguistics, and computer science, first-order logic (FOL), also called predicate logic, predicate calculus, or quantificational logic, is a type of formal system.

label: Fast-growing hierarchy
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Fast-growing hierarchy", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In computability theory, computational complexity theory and proof theory, a fast-growing hierarchy (also called an extended Grzegorczyk hierarchy, or a Schwichtenberg–Wainer hierarchy) is an ordinal-indexed family of rapidly increasing functions fα: N → N (where N is the set of natural numbers {0, 1, ...}, and α ranges up to some large countable ordinal).

label: Delta-functor
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Delta-functor", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In homological algebra, a δ-functor between two abelian categories A and B is a collection of functors from A to B together with a collection of morphisms that satisfy properties generalising those of derived functors.

label: Classical group
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Classical group", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the classical groups are the matrix groups arising from finite-dimensional vector spaces and from nondegenerate bilinear, sesquilinear, quadratic, and Hermitian forms.

label: Dual cone and polar cone
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Dual cone and polar cone", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Dual cone and polar cone are closely related concepts in convex analysis, a branch of mathematics.

label: Closure (mathematics)
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Closure (mathematics)", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, a subset of a larger set is closed under a given operation on the larger set if performing that operation on members of the subset always produces a member of that subset.

label: Big M method
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Big M method", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In operations research, the Big M method is a method of solving linear programming problems using the simplex algorithm.

sources.title: English Wikipedia article: Big M method

label: Barycentric subdivision
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Barycentric subdivision", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, the barycentric subdivision is a standard way to subdivide a given simplex into smaller ones.

label: Cauchy product
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Cauchy product", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mathematics, more specifically in mathematical analysis, the Cauchy product is the discrete convolution of two infinite series.

label: Alexandrov space
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Alexandrov space", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In differential geometry, Alexandrov spaces with curvature ≥ k form a generalization of Riemannian manifolds with sectional curvature ≥ k, where k is some real number.

label: Constant chord theorem
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Constant chord theorem", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: The constant chord theorem is a statement in elementary geometry about a property of certain chords in two intersecting circles.

sources.title: English Wikipedia article: Constant chord theorem

label: Collectively exhaustive events
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Collectively exhaustive events", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In probability theory and logic, a set of events is jointly or collectively exhaustive if at least one of the events must occur.

sources.title: English Wikipedia article: Collectively exhaustive events

label: Cantor–Bernstein theorem
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Cantor–Bernstein theorem", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In set theory and order theory, the Cantor–Bernstein theorem states that the cardinality of the second type class, the class of countable order types, equals the cardinality of the continuum.

label: Büchi–Elgot–Trakhtenbrot theorem
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Büchi–Elgot–Trakhtenbrot theorem", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In formal language theory, the Büchi–Elgot–Trakhtenbrot theorem states that a language is regular if and only if it can be defined by a formula in monadic second-order logic (MSO).
